name: Box64 dynarec: 2 MiB code block mapped PROT_READ|PROT_WRITE|PROT_EXEC and never flipped
component: Box64: addDBAlternateBlock / dynarec block allocator (custommem.c, DYNMMAPSZ path)
required_postconditions: the block is writable and executable at the same time: Box64 emits native code into it and branches into it without any mprotect step
setProtection_box records PROT_READ|PROT_WRITE|PROT_EXEC for the whole block, so Box64's own protection bookkeeping also assumes RWX is durable
the size is rounded to box64_pagesize, so a host with a larger page rounds the 2 MiB block up rather than failing

failure_sink.description: on MAP_FAILED it logs 'Cannot create dynamic map of %zu bytes' and returns 0; the caller degrades to no dynarec for that block rather than aborting.

source_locations.symbol: InternalMmap(NULL, allocsize, PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE | PROT_EXEC, MAP_ANONYMOUS | MAP_PRIVATE, -1, 0)

extraction_limitations: the MAP_HUGETLB variant immediately above (line 1796) is inside '#if 0//def MAP_HUGETLB' and is dead code at this commit; it is not modelled.
whether Box64 truly never flips protection on this block was established by the absence of an mprotect on the block address, not by proving the negative across all call sites.

x_campaign.rationale: The probe measured write_execute_simultaneous=true and jit_entitlement_required=false; plain anonymous RWX mmap works on stock x86-64 Linux without SELinux/PaX in enforcing mode.
